But the disclaimer here is that this is all work that was done before I went to Capital One, so they don't get to tell me what I can't say about this topic. So some of you may remember this issue, taking vector transposer seriously. How many of you have read this issue? Oh my goodness, OK. All right.
cues.zh: 我叫 Jiahao Chen。大约四个月前，我还在 MIT CSAIL 的 Julia Labs。我现在在纽约的 Capital One 工作。但先声明一下，这些都是我去 Capital One 之前做的工作，所以他们管不着我能不能谈这个话题。你们中有些人可能记得这个 issue：“认真对待向量转置”。有多少人读过这个 issue？天哪，好吧。行。

cues.en: Three quarters of you guys raised your hands. So the punch line here is that we were wrong on at least four counts on this issue. And I will explain as much as possible within half an hour why we were wrong. As you know, 4774 is quite possibly one of the most hotly debated issues of our time. And I went to sample some luminaries of our community to ask about their opinions. So here's one. Oh, sorry. Thank you. So here's one opinion.
cues.zh: 四分之三的人都举手了。所以重点是：在这个 issue 上，我们至少错了四点。我会尽量在半小时内解释清楚我们为什么错了。你们知道，4774 很可能是我们这个时代争论最激烈的问题之一。我还去问了我们社区里的一些大牛，想听听他们的看法。这儿有一个。哦，抱歉。谢谢。这里是一种观点。

cues.en: Here's another opinion from another luminary. And here's yet another opinion from that luminary who unfortunately could not be here and thus was born this issue. Surprisingly, it's not just us. So turns out that the Python people had also thought about this and they had, what is it? 381 comments on this particular issue. So this seems to be something that gets people riled up a lot. So let me introduce the surface problem.
cues.zh: 这是另一位大牛的观点。还有一位大牛的观点，可惜他本人没能到场，于是这个 issue 就诞生了。出乎意料的是，不只是我们。原来 Python 那边也想过这个问题，而且他们有，多少来着？这个 issue 有 381 条评论。所以这似乎是很能让人吵起来的事。下面我来介绍表面问题。

cues.en: This is what Julia 0.6 looks like. So here, I googled the first image for mathematician. And that is what I got. So I'm using that. So user comes in and says, I can't compute with Julia. I typed this. And it gave me a one element array. And then I tried to put in a more complicated expression, which I want to type. And it says, blah, blah, blah, blah, error. Sad. I am unhappy. Don't you know any mathematics?
cues.zh: 这就是 Julia 0.6 的样子。这里我谷歌了“数学家”的第一张图，就得到了这个。所以我就用这张。用户进来说：我没法用 Julia 算。我输入了这个，它给了我一个单元素数组。然后我试着输入一个更复杂的表达式，结果它说，吧啦吧啦吧啦，报错。难过。我不开心。你们 Julia 的人难道不懂数学吗？

cues.en: Oh, it's a little cut off. It says, don't you, Julia, people know any mathematics at the bottom. Our response here is, why would you want to do that? Why do people want to write inner products like this? And why do people get so worked up about this issue? So I did some research. And I've come to a conclusion that people don't know what vectors are. This issue exists because there are two slightly incompatible meanings of the word vector in mathematics. Here are the two definitions.
cues.zh: 哦，有点被截掉了。底部其实写着：你们 Julia 的人难道不懂数学吗？我们的回应是：你为什么想那样做？为什么人们想这样写内积？为什么大家会被这个问题搞得这么激动？所以我做了些研究。我得出结论：人们不知道向量是什么。这个 issue 之所以存在，是因为数学里“向量”这个词有两种略微不兼容的含义。下面是这两个定义。

cues.en: A vector is a column of a matrix. Second definition, a vector is that which has the algebra of a vector space. Not meant to be fortuitous tautology. Naturally isomorphic but not identical. These two vectors are similar but not identical. So a type one vector, a column of a matrix, clearly has the algebra of a vector space. However, not all vectors which have the algebra of a vector space are columns of matrices.
cues.zh: 向量是矩阵的一列。第二个定义：向量是具有向量空间代数结构的东西。这不是为了凑一个偶然的同义反复。它们自然同构，但并不相同。这两类向量相似，但不相同。所以第一类向量，也就是矩阵的一列，显然具有向量空间的代数结构。然而，并非所有具有向量空间代数结构的向量都是矩阵的列。

cues.en: On some level, this issue really is that simple. And I will refer to these two vectors as column vectors and flat vectors for the rest of this talk. I will be careful where possible to distinguish between these two uses of vector. But you might ask, why did we end up with two definitions of vector anyway? And it turns out, I read some books. And it turns out that this is what the history of linear algebra looks like.
cues.zh: 在某种程度上，这个问题确实就这么简单。接下来我会把这两类向量分别叫作列向量和扁平向量。我会尽量小心区分向量的这两种用法。但你可能会问：为什么我们最后会有两种向量定义？后来我读了一些书，发现线性代数的历史原来长这样。

cues.en: as simple as I've been able to make it. In short, sometime around 1924 to 1960, there was a division in the historical treatment of matrices and vectors. There was once a universe where matrices were their own subject and vectors were their own subject, and these two subjects did not mix whatsoever. And at some point, they merged. And we work in the world of the post-merger universe of matrices and vectors.
cues.zh: 也就是我能讲得最简单的版本。简而言之，大约在 1924 到 1960 年间，矩阵和向量的历史处理出现了分化。曾经有一个世界，矩阵是独立学科，向量也是独立学科，两者完全不相干。后来某个时刻，它们合并了。而我们现在所处的是矩阵和向量合并后的世界。

cues.en: Just some key moments in the history here. So we see that on the left-hand side, the matrix-only universe, we have things like, phrases like column matrix. We have the notation that many of us recognize today when we do linear algebra. On the vector side, we have the vector space axioms. We have the coordinate geometry. We have the notion of tuple. And at some point in the 1920s, the mathematicians said,
cues.zh: 这里只讲几个历史关键时刻。左边是只有矩阵的世界，我们会看到“列矩阵”这样的说法，还有今天很多人做线性代数时认得的记号。向量这边，有向量空间公理、坐标几何、元组的概念。到了 1920 年代的某个时刻，数学家们说，

cues.en: Oh, hey, column matrices form a vector space, and hence was born the other definition, which is both older and newer than the other definition. So if this is too complicated, I have tried to retell the story with emoji. There is a pre-unification era. There is the early unification era where you needed to explain this carefully. And then there's the era where it's also obvious you should have learned this in elementary school.
cues.zh: “哦，列矩阵构成一个向量空间。”于是另一种定义诞生了，它比另一种定义既更古老又更新。如果这太复杂，我试过用 emoji 重讲这个故事。有一个前统一时代；有一个早期统一时代，那时你还得仔细解释这件事；然后还有一个时代，它明显到你觉得小学就该学过。

cues.en: So what does this look like? So I pulled out one of these books and Van der Vaden's book on modern algebra is arguably the textbook that invented abstract algebra in its modern form. And what did he write about this? You will notice, first of all, that this is all not in German. It's in English. But nonetheless, I have a good authority that this survives from the first edition of the modern algebra textbook.
cues.zh: 那这到底是什么样？我翻出了其中一本书，Van der Vaden 的《Modern Algebra》可以说是发明了现代形式抽象代数的教科书。他关于这一点写了什么？首先你会注意到，这全都不是德语，而是英语。不过，我有可靠依据说，这段内容从《Modern Algebra》教科书第一版就保留了下来。

cues.en: that this is how he named all the things. So vectors were the abstract thing that had the algebra, and it is composed of coefficients, and the coefficients themselves form tuples. And by the way, you can assign to this vector a column matrix. So to recap,
cues.zh: 他就是这样给所有东西命名的。所以，向量是有代数结构的抽象对象，它由系数组成，而系数本身构成元组。顺便说，你可以给这个向量指派一个列矩阵。总结一下，

cues.en: The algebra is in the vector. The coefficients, which what we made today call ring elements, are just some numbers, some scalars. These are the things that define scalars. Two poles are indexable collections of these coefficients, these elements of a ring. But there's no algebra defined on them. And then by the way, there's this older topic called linear algebra that has column matrix. Warning again, most of these words are horribly, horribly overloaded.
cues.zh: 代数在向量里。系数——今天我们叫环元素——只是一些数、一些标量。这些就是定义标量的东西。元组是这些系数、这些环元素的可索引集合，但并没有在它们上面定义代数。顺便说，还有一门更老的学科叫线性代数，里面有列矩阵。再提醒一次：这些词大多被严重、严重地重载了。

cues.en: But I think this maybe gives you a sense of what mathematicians were thinking about when they talked about algebra and vectors in the context of vector spaces. Another book that I thought was really enlightening about this era comes from this book which has this awesome title called The Vectors of Mind. Multiple factor analysis for the isolation of primary traits. So this is actually a statistics textbook from 1935. And I think it explains very clearly how this evolution
cues.zh: 但我认为这也许能让大家大致了解，数学家在向量空间的语境下谈论代数和向量时，究竟在思考什么。另一本让我对那个时代深受启发的书，书名非常酷，叫《The Vectors of Mind: Multiple factor analysis for the isolation of primary traits》。这其实是一本1935年的统计学教材。我觉得它非常清晰地解释了这一演化

cues.en: made a transition from the isolated universe to the post-unification universe. So I will read a little bit of this. Basically that if a matrix has a single column, it is a column vector. If it has a single row, it is a row vector. And the vectorial terminology probably can be regarded as a consequence of geometry. So I think this is really, really the crux of the matter.
cues.zh: 是如何从彼此割裂的世界过渡到统一后的世界的。我来念一小段。大意是，如果一个矩阵只有一列，它就是列向量；如果只有一行，它就是行向量。而向量术语大概可以看作是几何学的结果。所以我觉得这才是真正、真正的关键所在。

cues.en: Fast forward to 1953 when the field of numerical analysis was invented, and this is the language and cornerstone of how all numerical analysts today speak matrix algebra. Most of you here may not be familiar with householder notation, so I will just summarize this very briefly. Essentially, there is a typographic convention where scalars are small Greek letters,
cues.zh: 快进到1953年数值分析领域创立，它是如今所有数值分析学者谈论矩阵代数的通用语言和基石。在座的大多数人可能不熟悉 Householder 记号，我先非常简略地概括一下。本质上，这是一种排版约定：标量用希腊小写字母，

cues.en: Vectors are small roman letters, and matrices are large roman letters. And you want to spell certain things as follows. For example, you might want an inner product, which you want to write as U prime times V, and now the product that's U times V prime, and then you have bilinear forms that look like U prime times A times V. And I would argue that just about every complicated expression involving matrices and vectors really come down to compositions of these elementary types of products.
cues.zh: 向量用罗马小写字母，矩阵用罗马大写字母。你可以像这样书写某些运算。比如内积写作 U prime 乘 V，外积写作 U 乘 V prime，还有形如 U prime 乘 A 乘 V 的双线性型。我认为，几乎所有涉及矩阵和向量的复杂表达式，归根结底都是这些基础乘积形式的组合。

cues.en: Now, the interesting thing here is that you only need two operations to express all of them. You only need the transpose and the multiplication. And there's a caveat here. Let me try that again. Sorry about that. So the caveat here is what exactly we mean by transpose and multiply. So let's dig into one of these things. It turns out that there is an assumption here about matrix algebra that is hidden in
cues.zh: 有趣的是，你只需要两种运算就能表达所有这些：转置和乘法。不过这里有个需要注意的地方。我重说一遍，不好意思。需要注意的地方在于，转置和相乘究竟是什么意思。让我们来深挖一下。事实证明，矩阵代数中隐藏着一个假设，它隐藏在

cues.en: the desire to write something like U prime times V being a product involving vectors and vectors returning a scalar. So I've tried to break it down in the way a computer scientist might and try to assign the meanings of various arrows here. So you see that what you do here is first of all you convert everything to matrices and then
cues.zh: 那种想把 U prime 乘 V 写成向量与向量相乘并返回一个标量的直觉背后。我尝试用计算机科学家的方式来拆解它，试着解释这里各个箭头的含义。你会看到，这里的做法首先是把所有内容都转换成矩阵，然后

cues.en: the regular definitions of matrix transpose and matrix multiply automatically hold, you don't need new definitions of what prime and star are in this case. So long as you are able to automatically convert between vectors and column matrices on the left hand side, and on the right hand side, a conversion between one by one matrices and true scalars, which are these coefficients of the field. So what's really missing here from this picture, which I will highlight explicitly, are these isomorphisms.
cues.zh: 常规的矩阵转置和矩阵乘法定义就自然成立了，你不需要为这种情况下的 prime 和乘号引入新定义。只要你能在左侧自动实现向量和列矩阵之间的转换，并在右侧实现 1x1 矩阵与真正标量（也就是数域中的系数）之间的转换。所以这张图中真正缺失的、也是我要重点强调的，就是这些同构关系。

cues.en: And it comes down to the crux, really, of whether or not you want your language to deal with these isomorphisms for you, or whether you want to deal with them yourself. That's the second version of the punchline. Julia, prior to 0.6, actually used this particular definition. So in the context of an inner product, what we said was the promotion from vector to matrix and matrix transpose is our definition of what a vector transpose is.
cues.zh: 归根结底，关键在于：你是希望由语言来替你处理这些同构关系，还是希望自己来处理它们。这就是这个核心结论的第二种表述。Julia 在 0.6 之前，实际上采用的就是这个特定定义。所以在内积的语境下，我们所说的是：将向量提升为矩阵，再对矩阵进行转置，这就是我们对向量转置的定义。

cues.en: The thing that results from this is that if you think about this expression as the composition of just transpose and multiply, that it's actually broken. And it's broken in a very bad way, because this is what happens inside in Julia 0.5 and earlier, that you promote the left-hand side vector to a matrix, then apply your transposition to get a row matrix,
cues.zh: 由此产生的结果是，如果你把这个表达式看作只是转置和乘法的组合，那它其实是有问题的。而且问题很严重，因为在 Julia 0.5 及更早版本内部发生的是：你把左侧向量提升成矩阵，然后应用转置得到一个行矩阵，

cues.en: And then you have a matrix vector product, which, of course, must return you a vector. And vectors are bad because you cannot divide by them. They don't have a scalar algebra. For example, that one by one matrices are actually much better at. You can do scalar operations with one by one matrices, and you just can't do very much with one vectors. And the result is unhappy Einstein. So there's other competing language that you may have heard about, MATLAB. I will argue that MATLAB is
cues.zh:
然后你会遇到矩阵向量乘积，当然，它必须返回一个向量。
而向量很糟糕，因为你不能除以向量。
它们没有标量代数。
比如，1×1 矩阵其实更擅长做这件事。
你可以用 1×1 矩阵做标量运算，而用一维向量你根本做不了多少事。
结果就是不高兴的爱因斯坦。
所以还有另一种竞争语言，你可能听说过，叫 MATLAB。
我会论证 MATLAB 是

cues.en: in anomaly in modern languages, and it's why we feel uncomfortable about some of its semantics. And it's because it's firmly rooted in type one vectors, which are columns. So two quotes from various documentation about MATLAB. The first one comes from the original matrix laboratory report from 1980 from the University of New Mexico, when Cleve Morlow was still faculty there. In MATLAB, the matrix is the only data type with scalars, vectors, and text as special cases.
cues.zh: 这是现代语言中的一个异常之处，也正是它的某些语义让我们感到不适的原因。因为它深深植根于第一类向量，而第一类向量是列向量。下面是 MATLAB 各种文档中的两段引文。第一段引自 1980 年新墨西哥大学发布的原始《矩阵实验室》报告，当时 Cleve Morlow 还是那里的教员。“在 MATLAB 中，矩阵是唯一的数据类型，标量、向量和文本都是它的特殊情况。”

cues.en: The second one comes from last year's MATLAB manual where it still says matrices with dimension equal to one on one side and e greater than one on the other side are called vectors. So now that we are primed to see that there are two definitions of vector, this is very clearly a type one vector that is being defined in MATLAB. So why doesn't MATLAB have this problem? It's because everything is a matrix and everything is coerced on demand to a vector or scalar as necessary.
cues.zh: 第二个来自去年的 MATLAB 手册，里面仍然说，一边维度等于 1、另一边维度大于 1 的矩阵称为向量。所以，既然我们现在已经意识到向量有两种定义，那么 MATLAB 中定义的显然就是第一类向量。那为什么 MATLAB 没有这个问题？因为一切都是矩阵，并且一切都会按需被强制转换成向量或标量。

cues.en: And some of you may know this as the trailing singleton dimension rule, where you can arbitrarily add or remove extra dimensions that have just length one at the end of an array in MATLAB. So what you see here is that our isomorphism simply become the addition and dropping of trailing indices as necessary. And furthermore,
cues.zh: 你们中有些人可能知道，这叫尾随单例维度规则：在 MATLAB 中，你可以随意在数组末尾添加或删除长度为 1 的额外维度。所以这里可以看到，我们的同构就变成了按需添加和删除尾随索引。而且，

cues.en: In MATLAB, you just stop at the one by one matrix expression. You don't need to convert it to a true scalar because that's good enough. And so this actually is a fairly elegant solution to the type one vector implementation. Why is this bad? It's not necessarily bad, but it's not really in line with how we think about dispatch because now you have to add these definitions to multiply that are shape based. So you have the special case
cues.zh:
在 MATLAB 中，你只需停留在 1×1 矩阵表达式这一步。  
你不需要把它转换成真正的标量，因为这样就已经够用了。  
所以，这实际上是类型一向量实现中一个相当优雅的解决方案。  
为什么这不好？  
它不一定不好，但这其实不太符合我们对分派的理解，因为现在你必须为乘法添加这些基于形状的定义。  
于是，你就有了这个特殊情况。

cues.en: one by one matrices on the left and one by one matrices on the right in order to get this to work the way you want it to. So to summarize, language design considerations, if you want to rely on just transpose and multiplication to write these expressions, you probably have to define transpose and multiply very carefully. And otherwise, you probably need special passing rules just to make this happen. Effectively, you're making something like blank prime star blank is really its own special operator.
cues.zh: 左边逐个矩阵，右边逐个矩阵，才能让它按你想要的方式工作。总结一下，语言设计上的考量是：如果你只想靠转置和乘法来写这些表达式，可能得把转置和乘法定义得非常仔细。否则，你可能需要特殊的传递规则才能做到这一点。实际上，你等于让“blank prime star blank”这种东西真正成为独立的特殊运算符。

cues.en: And this breaks composition, which may be very, very bad. If you think about accidentally introducing parentheses in the wrong place, you may get the wrong type as the result. And these kinds of special passing rules, as people like Jeff I'm sure will tell you, they add complexity to a language. And this is complexity for a very specific purpose, and it seems a little odd to do this. So what is the design space here? And it turns out that
cues.zh: 这会破坏组合性，而这后果可能非常严重。想想看，要是不小心在错误的位置加了括号，得到的结果类型可能就错了。而且这种特殊的传参规则，我相信像 Jeff 这样的人一定会告诉你，它们增加了语言的复杂度。而且这种复杂度纯粹是为了某个特定目的引入的，看起来有点怪。那么这里的语言设计空间是怎样的呢？结果发现——

cues.en: They're really only these two-by-two choices. If you only have scalars, matrices, and vectors in your language, then these are the two-by-two matrix, as it were, of the design choices. You can either have A times B which gives you a vector or a column matrix on the one end. And on the other hand, you can define the transpose of a vector to return you a row matrix or just itself.
cues.zh: 实际上就只有这 2x2 种选择。如果你的语言里只有标量、矩阵和向量，那么这些设计选择可以说就构成了一个 2x2 矩阵。一方面，A 乘以 B 可以返回一个向量或列矩阵；另一方面，你可以把向量的转置定义为返回一个行矩阵，或者直接返回它本身。

cues.en: And so this is what you get wrong if you want to insist on implementing householder notation. That in some quadrants, you get inner product wrong, which is us in old Julia. In another quadrant, you get outer product wrong. And the quadratic products and bilinear forms are wrong on the other side. So that's our main result here, that you can't have what you want. Thus, let's introduce the row vector. And it turns out that having a row vector
cues.zh: 所以如果你坚持要实现 Householder 记法，就会出现这些问题。在某些象限中，内积会出错，以前的旧版 Julia 就是这样。在另一个象限中，外积会出错。而在另一侧，二次型乘积和双线性形式又会出错。所以我们这里的核心结论就是，你不可能两全其美。因此，我们引入了行向量。事实证明，引入行向量

cues.en: combined with the type-based dispatch that we know have grown to love in Julia, actually can get everything to work. So the moral of the story is that you can't get what you want for a householder with three types, but you can with four. So what did everyone else do? And this is a really interesting slide, I think. I've gone through and looked at what other people do in this case.
cues.zh: 再结合大家在 Julia 中熟知且喜爱的基于类型的分派机制，其实就能让一切运转正常。所以结论就是：三种类型无法完美支持 Householder 记法，但四种类型就可以。那么其他语言是怎么做的呢？我觉得这张幻灯片很有意思。我调研了其他人面对这种情况时的做法。

cues.en: you can see that there's a wide variety of things you might do to vector transpose. Either it's an error, like in Lua. It can be the identity, like in NumPy, in Mathematica, and also in SciRuby. We have the old Julia behavior on one's hand, and we also have the new Julia behavior in yet another box. And it turns out that we're not alone in this box. There is this other language called
cues.zh: 你可以看到，对向量转置的处理方式多种多样。要么直接报错，比如 Lua；要么就是恒等变换，比如 NumPy、Mathematica 还有 SciRuby。一方面有旧版 Julia 的做法，另一方面新版 Julia 则在另一个格子里。而且事实证明，在这个格子里我们并不孤单。还有另一种语言叫作

cues.en: which is used in number theory calculations, which actually has this design. And furthermore, you have to explicitly convert between columns and matrices, and rows and matrices, and rows and columns. On the other hand, there's R, and R is actually a really interesting design quadrant here, because basically, the moment you do any linear algebra, the result is a matrix.
cues.zh: 它被用于数论计算，其实也采用了这种设计。而且，你必须在列和矩阵、行和矩阵，以及行和列之间进行显式转换。另一方面是 R，R 在这里其实是一个非常有意思的设计象限，因为基本上只要你做任何线性代数运算，得到的结果就都是矩阵。

cues.en: So on some level, this is actually really easy to understand. So once you invoke the matrix multiply operator or the transpose operator, you get a matrix. And arguably MATLAB sort of fits in this corner, but not really, since we've already discussed that MATLAB does not have true scalars or vectors. And then there are these little pieces here that nobody's explored, and maybe this is an avenue for new language design. So if you were interested in making your own language, you might want to try these out for yourself to see how you like them.
cues.zh: 所以从某种层面上看，这其实非常好理解。只要你调用了矩阵乘法运算符或转置运算符，就会得到一个矩阵。MATLAB 某种程度上也算在这一角，但又不完全是，因为我们之前讨论过 MATLAB 没有真正的标量或向量。此外，还有些小区域至今无人涉足，这或许是新语言设计的一个方向。所以如果你有兴趣自己做一门语言，不妨亲自尝试一下这些方案，看看效果如何。

cues.en: So how do row vectors work? We need new definitions of transpose and multiply, but then the actual expressions that you get is simpler, because all you do is just apply those two new definitions, and then you're done. So the question is, is this really that bad that we need more definitions? Probably not, because as you know, multiplication is already highly polymorphic in Julia. Just for the record, everything past the first method definition is font size 1.5.
cues.zh: 那么行向量是怎么工作的？我们需要重新定义转置和乘法，但这样一来，实际得到的表达式反而更简单，因为你只需要应用这两个新定义，然后就完成了。所以问题是：为了这些定义，真的需要付出这么大的代价吗？可能并不需要，因为你也知道，在 Julia 中，乘法本来就具有很强的多态性。顺便说明一下，从第一个方法定义之后的所有内容，字号都是 1.5。

cues.en: That's how many methods we have in Julia. But in some sense, there's a very natural analogy between how Julia organizes this kind of generic function system and how we learn how to do mathematics. So I don't think anyone really learned multiplication from complex numbers. I think all of us started from multiplication tables, which is int times int.
cues.zh:
这就是我们在 Julia 里拥有的方法数量。
但从某种意义上说，Julia 组织这种泛型函数系统的方式，与我们学习数学的方式之间有一个很自然的类比。
所以我不认为有人真的是从复数学会乘法的。
我想我们都是先从乘法表开始，也就是 int 乘以 int。

cues.en: Then maybe you graduate in school to go to fractions, and so you have rational times int. And then maybe you have real numbers and decimals, then you have real times real. Then if you stay in school long enough to learn more mathematics, you learn complex times complex, matrix times vector, and all this other fun stuff. So really just introducing new things like row vector times matrix, row vector times column vector, it's just more of the same. So that's a little bit of a hand-wavy justification of why this is not such a bad design. So the current...
cues.zh: 然后也许你在学校里学到分数，于是有了有理数乘整数。接着也许你学到实数和十进制小数，于是有了实数乘实数。再然后，如果你在学校待得够久、学了更多数学，你就会学到复数乘复数、矩阵乘向量，以及诸如此类好玩的东西。所以其实只是引入新东西，比如行向量乘矩阵、行向量乘列向量，本质上还是同一类操作。所以这算是一个有点粗略的论证，说明为什么这个设计还不算太糟。那么当前的……

cues.en: Excuse me. We don't really need the slide. Instead, I will skip forward to just a summary, and I'll leave plenty of time for questions. I'm sure you have many. First of all, I think we have taken vector transposer seriously at this point. And really, special credit really has to go to Andy Ferris, who is here somewhere, right? Where are you? Please give this man a round of hand.
cues.zh: 不好意思。我们其实不需要幻灯片。我直接跳到总结部分，并留出充足时间提问。我相信你们有很多问题。首先，我觉得到这一步，我们已经认真对待 vector transposer 了。特别要感谢 Andy Ferris，他就在现场某处，对吧？你在哪儿？请给这位先生一轮掌声。

cues.en: As you know, it was my privilege as an academic to just speculate about what to do, but Andy actually did it. So that also deserves plenty of credit. So really, what I've learned from this is that we were all wrong about vectors. And we have forgotten what used to be difficult. We've forgotten that we used to have to worry about these isomorphisms explicitly. We have this incompatible definitions of columns
cues.zh: 如你所知，作为学者，我有幸只需推测该怎么做，但 Andy 真正把它做出来了。所以这也值得大加赞赏。所以实际上，我从中学到的是，我们对向量的看法全错了。而且我们忘了过去哪些东西很难。我们忘了以前不得不显式地操心这些同构。我们对列有这些互不兼容的定义。

cues.en: of column vectors and flat vectors, we've forgotten that multiplication is actually this inherently overloaded and polymorphic operation. And one new result here is that you need at least four types to do householder notation in a type-based dispatch system. And I will leave it at here and take any questions you may have. Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 对于列向量和扁平向量，我们遗忘了乘法本质上是一种重载且多态的操作。这里的最新成果之一是，在基于类型的分派系统中实现 Householder 记号，至少需要四种类型。我就讲到这里，接下来欢迎大家提问。非常感谢。
